answer:
The feature is **iterative index scans**, available starting in pgvector 0.8.0. The README says:

"Starting with 0.8.0, you can enable iterative index scans, which will automatically scan more of the index until enough results are found (or it reaches `hnsw.max_scan_tuples` or `ivfflat.max_probes`)." [pgvector/README.md]

It explains the cause as well: "queries with filtering can return less results since filtering is applied *after* the index is scanned." [pgvector/README.md]

To enable it for HNSW, the README gives this setting, which keeps results in exact distance order: "SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order;" [pgvector/README.md]

For IVFFlat, the README shows "SET ivfflat.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;". Relaxed ordering can return results slightly out of distance order in exchange for better recall. [pgvector/README.md]
